query: If the most common operational burdens described in the text were eliminated, how much would resolution duration drop?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents from short_description gives a strong axis to group operational burdens and compare resolution durations. Values (network_connectivity, vpn_access, database, printing) match source text soundly.

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: Failure mode is a genuine analytical axis distinct from category. Values are well-warranted readings (connectivity_failure for WiFi/VPN, access_denial for 'unable to access database'), and silent rows correctly get Unknown/NULL.

per_column.name: affected_system_scope
per_column.rationale: Useful axis for locating burden. But scope is partly inferred beyond the text: 'Cannot connect to office WiFi' and VPN labeled 'infrastructure' is defensible, yet 'online database' as server_side and printing as client_side are inferences the terse text only weakly supports, so groundedness is moderate.

per_column.name: reassignment_indicator
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is highly relevant as an operational burden affecting duration. However, the short_description/opened_at/closed_by text carries no evidence of reassignment; true/false values (403/97) appear invented and not derivable from the sampled source fields.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (496 true / 4 false) so it offers almost no analytical leverage. Recurrence is also not derivable from a single row's terse text; the near-uniform 'true' appears fabricated.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Individual vs system_wide is a useful burden axis, but largely redundant with affected_system_scope and weakly grounded: labeling WiFi/VPN issues 'individual' vs database 'individual' is inconsistent guesswork not clearly supported by text.

per_column.name: time_of_day_band
per_column.rationale: Derived directly from opened_at timestamps, a legitimate axis for whether off-hours load drives duration. Mostly sound, though 7:34 labeled business_hours and 8:50 business_hours vs 18:14 after_hours are reasonable bandings.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with existing assigned_to/closed_by columns. Values also contradict source: row 1 closed_by 'Fred Luddy' but sampled rows show assigned_agent differing from closed_by (e.g. VPN row assigned Beth Anglin while closed_by is Charlie), suggesting an ungrounded remapping.

per_column.name: caller_segment
per_column.rationale: Named a 'segment' but values are just individual caller names, offering little grouping leverage and duplicating caller_id. There is no caller field in the sampled source text, so the specific names appear ungrounded.

judge.rationale: Several columns give genuine axes for the 'operational burden vs duration' query: incident_category, failure_type, and time_of_day_band are both useful and well-grounded in short_description and opened_at. However a substantial subset is weak: recurrence_signal is near-constant and fabricated, reassignment_indicator asserts a fact the sampled text cannot support, assigned_agent and caller_segment are redundant restatements of existing columns and additionally contradict/lack source evidence, and scope_indicator overlaps affected_system_scope with shaky grounding. Overall the set offers moderate analytical leverage but notable hallucination in the process/behavioral columns drags groundedness below acceptable.
